statements.t: Our dedicated and knowledgeable team serves a diverse range of commercial and residential construction projects worldwide, guaranteeing outstanding products and seamless installation services.

Our track record of successfully delivering high profile projects has earned us an increasing number of opportunities across the United States, evidenced by our expanding backlog and overall revenue growth.

On April 3, 2025, we completed the acquisition of certain assets and assume certain liabilities of Continental Glass Systems, LLC, a leading provider of architectural glass and glazing solutions in the Southeast U.S., that included manufacturing equipment, intangibles, and a strong project backlog, enhancing our U.S. presence, customer reach, and supply chain efficiency.
Revenues from the commercial market rose 30.9% or $45.4 million year over year, as we continue to execute our growing project backlog.
The increase was driven by higher U.S. commercial market revenues, up $95.5 million, or 22.4% year over year, as we continue to execute on our growing backlog of projects.

We anticipate that the Company will continue to generate positive cashflow from operating activities throughout the remainder of the year, which we believe, in addition to our current liquidity position, provides ample flexibility to service our obligations through the next twelve months.

Investments made during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were mainly related to an ongoing broad automation project to increase efficiency, improve headcount and increase capacity given the Company´s current growth.
The Company expects the resulting increase in output to improve efficiency throughout its operations while reducing material waste, reducing headcount and improving overall lead times.

During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we paid $118.7 million to acquire property plant and equipment, reflecting scheduled payments for previously initiated projects and advance payments for ongoing projects focused on expanding capacity and improving operational efficiency.
Together, these actions are making us a stronger and more efficient company, and we remain confident in our ability to unlock additional value for our shareholders.”

Christian Daes, Chief Operating Officer of Tecnoglass, added, “Our backlog reached another record of $1.43 billion, extending our track record of sequential growth since 2021 and reflecting consistent execution on a growing pipeline of multi-family and commercial projects.

We continued to book large projects within the luxury lodging and condo market, and subsequent to quarter end signed our largest project to date, which continues to provide strong visibility for the next few years.

Our May pricing will reach multi-family and commercial revenue as projects booked after the increase move through our backlog, starting with shorter-cycle jobs late this year and larger projects during 2027.

In single-family residential projects, our expanding dealer network, vinyl lines and geographic diversification continue to support market share gains, and our recently opened Los Angeles showroom is bringing our Legacy Line to the West Coast.
Across both businesses, our differentiated product portfolio, expanding geographic reach, and strong project pipeline position us well to keep gaining share as we move into 2027.”
The Company has secured state, local and utility incentives that, should the project meet its parameters, are expected to significantly enhance the estimated returns of the potential project.

Santiago Giraldo, Chief Financial Officer of Tecnoglass, stated, “Based on our performance year to date and the visibility provided by our order book, we are raising our full year 2026 revenue outlook to a range of $1.10 billion to $1.14 billion and adjusting our Adjusted EBITDA outlook to a range of $210 million to $220 million.
The change in our Adjusted EBITDA outlook mainly reflects the approximately $8.4 million non-cash inventory revaluation in the third quarter.
Excluding that effect, our Adjusted EBITDA outlook would have been approximately $8.4 million higher.
